title: Second order and secondary functional renormalization group flow equations
summary: The functional renormalization group provides a powerful non-perturbative framework for quantum field theory through the exact flow equation for the scale-dependent effective action. A mass-type regulator $R_k = k^2$ is particularly attractive because it preserves symmetries, locality, and unitarity (or Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity in the Euclidean domain). However, unlike momentum-dependent regulators, it does not tame all ultraviolet divergences: in four dimensions, flow equations for the effective potential exhibit logarithmic divergences. Motivated by Callan's perturbative renormalization scheme, where higher-order $\theta$-insertions improve ultraviolet convergence, we develop two classes of higher-order functional flow equations. First, we derive exact second-order flow equations by taking further derivatives of the standard flow equation with respect to $k$. These have either a one-loop structure involving the first derivative of the inverse propagator, or a mixed one-loop and two-loop structure. While exact and useful for incorporating two-loop effects and testing truncation schemes, they do not in general resolve the ultraviolet convergence problem. Second, we introduce a secondary flow method, where variations of an effective mass-squared parameter introduce an additional flow, with parameter $l$. The resulting secondary flow equations become ultraviolet finite once sufficiently many derivatives have been taken, and can be evaluated without an additional ultraviolet regulator. Integrating back to the standard flow requires integration constants that encode microscopic ultraviolet physics, analogous to relevant coupling constants.

title: Spectrum of a 2D QFT analogue of the SYK model
summary: We study the spectrum of the two-dimensional generalisation of the SYK model proposed by Turiaci and Verlinde, in which chiral Majorana fermions with a topological kinetic term interact through random $2q$-fermion couplings. We compute the four-point function at order $1/N$ in the conformal limit. In addition to the conformal Casimir, the ladder kernels commute with the operator that exchanges a single lightcone coordinate. As a result, the four-point function splits into an even and an odd sector, which the kernels do not mix. In each sector we construct a complete eigenbasis of the Casimir, find the eigenvalues of the kernels in closed form and sum the ladder diagrams. The poles in the ladder sum lie on a spectral curve in the plane of the two conformal weights. A conformal solution in the IR limit breaks the symmetries of the model under chiral reparametrisations and local Lorentz transformations, and the kernel has eigenvalue one on the corresponding modes. The reparametrisation modes, with conformal weights $(2,0)$ and $(0,2)$, are non-normalisable, whereas the Lorentz mode of the odd sector, with weights $(1,1)$, is normalisable. We determine the region where the sum of ladders can be represented in a contour form analogous to that of the one-dimensional SYK model.

title: Modular Structure of the ADHM Effective Twisted Superpotential
summary: The Cardy limit of M2-brane indices retains nonperturbative information through the effective twisted superpotential, including corrections exponentially suppressed at large rank. We investigate the flavor dependence of these corrections in the three-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ $\mathrm U(N)$ ADHM theory at the universal twist. For $N_f=1,2,4$ fundamental hypermultiplets, we conjecture that the full exponential remainder of the selected Bethe critical value is an absolutely convergent divisor sum obtained by applying a first-order differential operator to an Eichler integral of a weight-four Eisenstein form. Resolving this remainder requires the additive constant, which we evaluate from its known integral representation as finite Clausen sums for every positive integer $N_f$. Expanding the integral together with the shifted-rank power determines the type-IIA coefficients of the perturbative contribution at arbitrary genus and their factorial growth. With this subtraction fixed, the proposed sums reproduce independently computed Bethe critical values at up to $800$-digit accuracy, including low ranks that test the continuation beyond the reconstructed sectors. The flavor-one expression agrees with level-one ABJM, whereas the two- and four-flavor completions have distinct divisor laws related by exact dissection identities to finite combinations of ABJM functions. The comparison supports a shared weight-four organization of nonperturbative Bethe data beyond the mirror pair, with arithmetic that distinguishes the theories. Through the finite-rank Cardy relation, the proposed completion predicts the entire $1/\omega$ coefficient of the selected vacuum contribution to the superconformal index, retaining these theory-dependent corrections in its leading exponent.

title: Mirror symmetry of $\mathcal{N}=(0,4)$ boundary conditions with Nahm poles
summary: We propose mirror symmetry between $\mathcal{N}=(0,4)$ boundary conditions with Nahm poles and Neumann boundary conditions with boundary Fermi multiplets in 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ non-Abelian gauge theories, including $U(N)$ SQCD, $T[SU(N)]$ and the ADHM theories. We obtain the half-indices of the Nahm pole boundary conditions from those of the Dirichlet boundary conditions by Higgsing, where the boundary fugacities are specialized along the principal embedding of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. We check that they agree with the half-indices of the dual Neumann boundary conditions. In the twist limits they give closed-form formulas for the vacuum characters of the boundary vertex operator algebras of Costello and Gaiotto. We find that the unflavored vacuum characters are eta-quotients times quasimodular forms, which we write explicitly in terms of Eisenstein series for all our examples.

title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
summary: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

title: Destabilization of Abelian-Higgs vortices at large Chern-Simons coupling
summary: We study the effect of the Chern--Simons (CS) coupling on the radial spectral stability of axially symmetric vortices in the $(2+1)$-dimensional Abelian--Higgs model. From the linear stability approach, we obtain the dispersion relations of gauge field perturbations, which signal the existence of a critical CS coupling $k_{\rm c}$ that depends on Maxwell's coupling constant. For $k<k_{\rm c}$, the continuous spectrum is purely imaginary and the modes remain gapped. At $k=k_{\rm c}$, one of the modes becomes gapless, while for $k>k_{\rm c}$ real eigenvalues appear, corresponding to exponentially growing radial modes. Direct time-evolution simulations are consistent with the spectral analysis, which shows instability for $k>k_{\rm c}$. Below the threshold, the perturbed vortex relaxes toward its stationary profile, whereas above the threshold, growing fluctuations deform the core and propagate outward. These results show that the CS coupling controls radial spectral stability of Abelian-Higgs vortices, and destabilization occurs for sufficiently large CS coupling, relative to the Maxwell coupling.

title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

title: Gravitational Corrections to OPE Coefficients
summary: The short-distance singular behavior of correlation functions of quantum field theories in curved spacetime is a universal property shared by all well-behaved states (known as Hadamard states). For two-point functions this takes the form of the Hadamard tail of free scalars and its generalizations to spinning fields and interacting theories. In this work, we compute similar universal curvature corrections to curved-space OPE coefficients in a short-distance expansion for interacting quantum field theories in general dimensions. We work at leading order in the curvature but for arbitrary backgrounds. Examples include weakly coupled scalar field theories with cubic and quartic interactions as well as strongly coupled conformal field theories. The gravitationally dressed OPE coefficients allow us to test explicitly, and confirm, the validity of the smearing-in-time procedure discussed by Witten in the construction of the algebra of observables near an observer's worldline in curved spacetime.

title: Exploring M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$: Mellin amplitudes with composite operators
summary: We bootstrap mixed correlators in M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$, focusing on tree-level correlation functions involving one double-particle operator and three single-particle operators. Combining inputs from AdS/CFT, the chiral algebra, and the OPE at large central charge, we uniquely determine the Mellin amplitude for $\langle [{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{q}]{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{p}{\cal O}_{p+q-2}\rangle$ for generic $p$ and $q$. While our main focus is the $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT in six dimensions, we also derive the analogous result in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, applying the same bootstrap approach to $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. Despite their different dynamics, the resulting Mellin amplitudes exhibit a strikingly similar structure, with non-trivial OPE predictions for low-twist protected operators providing a key input. Our work is motivated by recent developments in the study of Kaluza-Klein correlators in bubbling geometries, where four-point functions involving single- and multi-particle operators are computed as response functions to smooth deformations of the vacuum geometry. While well tested in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, we aim to extend this framework to M-theory.

title: The Spectral Anatomy of Complex-Time Singularities
summary: The properties of the bulk spacetime in a holographic theory may be probed by the analytic structure of the boundary correlator $G(t,x)$. In this letter, we analyse the singularities of $G(t,x)$ by deriving them from Fourier space. We show that the quasinormal modes are characterised by two distinct momentum scaling regimes. The first regime is defined by a finite $k/\omega^\gamma$ for some characteristic exponent $\gamma$ which is extracted from the singularity, and probes $G(t,0)$, reproducing the bouncing geodesic analysis. The second regime is defined by a finite $k/\omega$, and probes the complexified bulk away from the singularity, which allows us to study the singularities of $G(t,x\neq 0)$. We extract coefficients and exponents of the singularities for general spacetime dimensions, and allow for more exotic interiors. The heavy reliance of our computation on quasinormal modes opens the doors to a similar analysis being done on spacetimes that are accessible only numerically.

title: Geometric Quantization of the Giant Graviton Master Moduli Space
summary: We describe a remarkable reorganization of the space of gauge invariant operators of free or twisted $U(N)$ gauge theories as combinations of single-trace and determinant operators modulo certain "open loop equations". The reorganization has a transparent holographic interpretation, describing how states at finite $N$ can be reproduced by imposing certain $N$-independent gauge constraints on the combination of the closed strings Fock space and a geometric quantization of the moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes, with quantization parameter $N^{-1}$. The moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes is reproduced from tachyon condensation of auxiliary D-brane/anti-D-brane pairs which are "Koszul dual" to the D-brane system which supports the original gauge theory. We describe how to impose the open loop equations via certain BRST complexes and conjecture that their homology recovers the finite $N$ BPS Hilbert space in the limit of large auxiliary rank. The BRST construction conjecturally categorifies Murthy's Giant Graviton Expansion of indices counting $U(N)$-invariant BPS operators.

title: From pure spinor modules to superspace superfields
summary: We relate the pure spinor formalism to the superspace description of constrained superfields and gauge multiplets, mainly for abelian two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry, with three- and four-dimensional N=1 examples for comparison. For each multiplet we give an explicit module over the supertranslation Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra and match its reconstruction with the known superfields. First-order constraints come from modules supported on linear subspaces of the nilpotence variety, and higher-order ones, such as the complex-linear constraint, from Yoneda products of their Ext classes. Requiring a connection to act on given matter and its conjugate restricts its curvature, which yields the ordinary, twisted and semichiral vector multiplets with their field strengths. The module of each vector multiplet is the fiber product over the origin of the coordinate rings of the matter supports: its potentials are differences of partial potentials, and its gauge parameters are the matter superfields. For the large vector multiplet this fiber product is not a quotient of the pure spinor ring; its field strengths are four odd semichiral superfields, and partial regluing gives its constrained versions.

title: Resurgence without the Borel Plane: Mellin-Barnes Summation and Analytic Stokes Reconstruction
summary: We develop a route to resurgence without the Borel plane: sums of divergent perturbative series and their encoded nonperturbative monodromy are constructed directly in complex perturbative order. In the Analytic Umbral Framework (AUF), an analytic coefficient clock produces the sum through a Mellin-Barnes integral and its monodromy through a bare inverse Mellin transform. Neither a Borel transform nor continuation of a Borel germ is required for this construction. For Watson-admissible Gevrey clocks, the completion agrees with the canonical Borel-Laplace sum in the guaranteed directions. When the admissible aperture exceeds $2\pi$, the clockwise difference of adjacent logarithmic determinations is given by $2\pi i$ times the inverse-Mellin carrier. This carrier is also the AUF completion of a null clock and is flat on the overlap. The sum and its aggregate monodromy are thus obtained ''in one shot'', before resolving individual actions and fluctuation series. Euler's equation, zero-dimensional quartic models, the scaled Gamma function and a solvable $O(4)$ toy model exemplify the procedure, and show how further analysis recovers directional Stokes variations. The lognormal benchmark extends the construction beyond every finite Gevrey order: no finite-order Borel transform gives a convergent germ, yet explicit clock-selection conditions yield an AUF completion and a nonzero ordinary flat carrier. Distributed relaxation supplies a physical realization of this growth class. AUF therefore both reconstructs familiar resurgent information without Borel-plane continuation and extends completion beyond finite-order Borel-Laplace summation.

title: Algebra-Valued Yang-Mills-Type Theories: Polynomial Obstructions and Holonomy Reductions
summary: We study algebra-valued Yang-Mills-type ($A$-YMT) theories on a smooth $n$-manifold $M$, where connections take values in an $\mathfrak{m}$-graded algebra $(A, *)$ and descend to an associated bundle $E_A = P \times_\rho A \to M$. We derive the field equations, gauge transformations, and generalized Bianchi identities, showing that affine Ehresmann compatibility forces the vertical image of $\mathfrak{g}$ into the Lie nucleus $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Lie}}(A)$ of $[x,y]_* = x*y - y*x$, and that gauge covariance and the Bianchi identity are obstructed precisely by the Jacobiator $\mathrm{Jac}_{[\cdot,\cdot]_*}$ (leaving principal $G$-gauge symmetries anomaly-free). We then prove obstructions in three settings. First, internal-product Chern-Weil and self-dual $A$-YMT functionals vanish in weak $(2,s)$-solvable algebras, invariant under $(Q,S)$-splitting extensions. Second, in reductive Cartan-Yang-Mills theories on $A = \mathbb{R}^k \oplus \mathfrak{h}$, quartic-block parenthesization yields a strict cutoff at $n \ge 8$, while binary-tree halving yields an exact Jacobsthal-number cutoff ($n - 4 \notin \bigcup_{r \ge 3}\{2 J_r, J_{r+1}\}$, plus rank vanishing for $n \ge k + 5$). We catalog Berger holonomy reductions for $4 \le n \le 7$, proving an on-shell vanishing (torsion-free) vs. off-shell survival (torsionful) dichotomy in 4D for $U(2)$ and $SU(2)$ connections---via $e \curlywedge_\rtimes (e \curlywedge_\rtimes \Omega_\omega) = \frac{1}{2}(e \curlywedge_\rtimes e) \curlywedge_\rtimes \Omega_\omega$---and in 7D for $G_2$-connections. Third, we prove an associator-quotient collapse and Jacobiator vertex dichotomy for odd-dimensional internal $A$-Chern-Simons theories, with applications to $A$-$BF$ theories, octonionic and reductive Higgs Proca mass spectra, and reductive dualities.

title: Toward a Holographic Representation Theory of the Bosonic de Sitter Discrete Series
comment: 27 pages. Contribution to the proceedings of the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics (Group36), Valladolid, Spain, 2026
summary: We propose a program toward a holographic representation theory of the non-scalar bosonic discrete series $\Pi^\pm_{p,q}$, $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$, $1\leqslant q\leqslant p$, of the de Sitter ($\mathrm{dS}_{4}$) group $G=\mathrm{SO}_0(1,4)$. The proposal exploits two complementary realizations of the same unitary irreducible representation (UIR): a bounded-domain realization on an open ball $\mathbb{B}$ modeling the hyperbolic space $G/\mathrm{SO}(4)$, with $\partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, and a covariant spacetime realization on $\mathrm{dS}_{4}$, with conformal boundaries $\mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, in which the physical UIR is obtained through the corresponding gauge reduction. This leads to two boundary constructions and an explicit compatibility problem, \begin{align*} \mathbb{B} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \quad\overset{?}{\simeq}\quad \mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \mathrm{dS}_{4} \,. \end{align*} The two outer problems seek explicit intertwiners between the bulk and boundary realizations, with their invariant norms, constraints, and physical quotients properly identified. The middle problem asks how to construct and normalize a unitary intertwiner between the two boundary realizations once both have been shown to carry the same UIR. The bounded picture exposes the unitary and harmonic structure of the representation, while the spacetime picture makes its covariant and gauge-theoretic structure manifest, allowing the two constructions to constrain and illuminate one another. The established scalar family $\Pi_{p,0}$, $p\in\mathbb{N}$, with its spherical realization on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, provides the guiding prototype. Particular attention is given to ...

title: Baryon and lepton asymmetries across the cosmic QCD transition: effects of a 3D first-order surface
summary: We investigate the cosmological QCD phase transition by calculating the cosmic trajectories from the five equations that impose the conservation of the baryon and lepton asymmetries, the charge neutrality of the Universe, and $\beta$ equilibrium. We perform the calculation using for the first time the four-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q, \mu_S)$ Constant Entropy Contour equation of state, which for $\mu_S = 0$ ($\beta$-equilibrium) features a critical line and a first-order phase transition (FOPT) surface in the three-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q)$ space. We first show that, within the standard cosmological scenario with baryon asymmetry $b_{\text{obs}}=8.65\cdot 10^{-11}$, the lepton asymmetries alone can never induce a FOPT. We then explore the non-standard cosmological scenario with large values of $b$ and find that reaching a FOPT requires $b\gtrsim0.028$ during the QCD epoch. Such a value is compatible with observations only if the baryon asymmetry is diluted to $b_{\text{obs}}$ after the transition, which a period of little inflation would provide with $N\approx6.5$ $e$-folds of expansion. Finally, we study the phenomenological imprints on the equation of state and primordial black hole (PBH) formation, showing that pion condensation at large lepton asymmetries drives $c_s^2 > 1/3$ and shifts the PBH peak to sub-solar masses ($0.3-0.8\,M_\odot$), while the large-$b$ FOPT yields a narrow spike around $4.2\,M_\odot$.

title: Positivity Bounds, Negative Running, and the Weak Gravity Conjecture
summary: We study causality and unitarity constraints at one loop on a low-energy effective theory containing a photon, a massless scalar coupled to it through dilaton-like interactions, and a light neutral Dirac fermion with a Yukawa coupling to the scalar. In this setup, non-gravitational loop effects induced by the Yukawa interaction can drive the coefficient of the four-photon $(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})^2$ operator negative at low energies, apparently violating the tree-level positivity bound. Nevertheless, we find that these negative values are consistent with one-loop constraints from causality and unitarity, thanks to the low-energy contribution from the massless scalar to the relevant dispersion relation. We also examine the implications of this negative running for the Weak Gravity Conjecture in the magnetic limit of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes, since the RG-evolved Wilson coefficients can a priori shift the extremality condition towards the subextremal region. We find, however, that this shift is obstructed by the fermion mass induced by the same Yukawa coupling, which prevents the fermion from contributing to the running of the relevant operators down to the low-energy scales required to make the black holes subextremal. Finally, we discuss the relevance of negative running to loop-level positivity bounds in the SMEFT and to light-by-light scattering in the presence of a light scalar.

title: Geometric Bounds on Axion-Photon Couplings in Non-Supersymmetric Heterotic Compactifications
summary: We study the photon couplings of QCD axions and axion-like particles in non-supersymmetric heterotic string theory on Calabi-Yau threefolds with line bundles. After the Stückelberg mechanism and anomaly matching are taken into account, the QCD axion direction is determined by the QCD axion-coupling coefficients together with the axion kinetic matrix. We focus on the electromagnetic-to-color axion coupling ratio, $E/N$. When the physical electromagnetic and QCD axion-coupling vectors are proportional with the ratio fixed by the gauge levels, the QCD axion has $E/N=8/3$ for $k_3=k_2=1$ and $k_Y=5/3$, independently of the axion kinetic matrix. It is found that direct flux breaking of the visible $SO(16)_{\rm v}$ can produce independent QCD and electromagnetic axion-coupling vectors for the same level assignment. The Hermitian Yang-Mills equations and the heterotic Bianchi identity then restrict the departure from $8/3$. We derive analytic bounds for backgrounds with and without five-brane charge under assumptions about the axion kinetic terms and low-energy matching. An $SU(5)$-like model and a direct-flux Standard-Model-like model illustrate proportional and independent Green-Schwarz coupling vectors, respectively. For axions with no QCD coupling, we derive a geometric upper bound on their photon couplings and evaluate it in an explicit compactification.

title: Projection of massive and interacting conformal theories to the future null infinity
summary: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a Møller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.

title: Metastable vortex string decay in a brane picture
summary: We describe the decay of a metastable string as a bounce in a brane configuration. We consider a particular $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric $\mathrm{U}(2)$ gauge theory with cascade Higgsing $\mathrm{U}(2)\to \mathrm{U}(1)^2 \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, where the vortex string can break by creating a pair of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole and anti-monopole. The theory is engineered in a Type IIA brane setup, where the metastable string is realized as a D2-brane stretched between NS5- and D4-branes. The string breaks when the endpoints of the D2-brane, moving along the NS5- and D4-branes, meet so that the D2-brane shrinks to nothing. We check that the tension of the D2-brane reproduces that of the vortex string obtained numerically in the field theory, with the ratio approaching one in the limit where the vortex string becomes BPS. Within the thin-wall approximation, we derive the bounce action from the Dirac-Born-Infeld action of the D2-brane and find that it agrees with that of the field theory, with the monopole mass given by the area swept by the D2-brane. As a consistency check, we numerically construct a bounce solution of the D2-brane equation of motion under simplifying assumptions, whose action agrees with the thin-wall result in the regime where our description is reliable.

title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Plebański--Demiański spacetimes
summary: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arXiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arXiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arXiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.

title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
summary: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$. At $t=m=0$, the boundary contribution is power infrared divergent in four dimensions. Analytic continuation in DR conceals this divergence, which gives no $1/\epsilon$ pole about $d=4$. At the critical dimension $d=6$, the same endpoint diverges logarithmically and gives a pole in the continued integral. Nonzero $t$ and finite $m$ regulate the same boundary region, yielding the known anomaly-related $1/t$ pole and a previously unreported $1/m^2$ behavior, respectively. We also show that a transverse gluon-polarization projector can eliminate an anomaly-related contribution that survives with explicit gluon polarization vectors. Finally, we present complete one-loop results for polarized and unpolarized DDVCS with all three infrared prescriptions. After summing the diagrams, the same evolution kernel governs the infrared pole in DR and the logarithms $\ln(Q^2/(-t))$ and $\ln(Q^2/m^2)$ within each polarization channel. This work establishes the common geometric origin of these anomaly-related poles within one-loop box amplitudes.

title: Emerging understanding of the rare kaon decay $K^+\toπ^+\ell^+\ell^-$ from lattice QCD
comment: 7 Pages for main text, and 9 Pages for Supplementary Materials
summary: Rare kaon decays provide sensitive probes of the Standard Model and potential new physics. For $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$, the experimental decay rate determines only the squared vector form factor $|V(z)|^2$, leaving its sign undetermined. Previous lattice QCD calculations have either used unphysical pion masses or suffered from uncertainties too large to resolve this sign. Here we present a first-principles calculation using two domain-wall fermion ensembles with near-physical pion masses. We develop a computational strategy that establishes the ultraviolet finiteness and continuum equivalence of local and conserved vector currents, substantially simplifying the calculation of nonlocal matrix elements. Four independent subtraction schemes provide nontrivial consistency checks, while the one-end trick reduces noise from quark-self-loop contributions. We determine $V(z)$ at six spacelike and timelike momentum transfers. Fits consistently yield $V(0)<0$, with a statistical significance of $5.8\sigma$--$7.9\sigma$ at $M_{\eta_c}=1.1,\mathrm{GeV}$. After extrapolation to the physical charm-quark mass, the negative sign persists across all fit forms, with a significance of $2.0\sigma$--$3.4\sigma$. Our results provide direct first-principles evidence favoring the negative-sign solution and establish a framework for more precise lattice QCD determinations.

title: The ratio of gradient-flow scales $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0$ in $2+1$ flavor lattice QCD
summary: We determine the ratio $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0$ of gradient-flow scales in isospin-symmetric $2+1$-flavor QCD at the physical point and in the continuum limit. Our analysis uses CLS gauge ensembles at five lattice spacings and combines Wilson and Zeuthen flow data to constrain the continuum extrapolation at the flavor-SU(3)-symmetric point. We obtain $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0=0.8264(26)$ in the Edinburgh consensus scheme, corresponding to a precision of about $0.31\%$. This result relates determinations quoted in terms of either flow scale and helps assess tensions among published results.

title: Light baryon masses from the modified Taylor coupling
summary: We present a calculation of the positive-parity baryon octet and decuplet spectra, using a non-perturbative interaction governed by the modified Taylor effective charge and complemented by explicit flavour-dependent contributions. The framework transitions seamlessly from the mesonic domain, where it was first established, to the baryonic sector, requiring no further parameter optimization. By solving the relativistic three-body Faddeev equation, we extract both the ground-state masses and amplitudes for the corresponding baryonic configurations. The resulting spectrum reproduces experimental data within a few percent. Additionally, we derive the evolution of the nucleon and $\Delta$ masses as functions of the pion mass, contrast our findings directly against lattice-QCD benchmarks, and evaluate the propagation of the lattice uncertainties into the computed hadronic observables.

title: Towards an improved understanding of $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors
summary: The isovector axial-vector and tensor meson states $a_1$ and $a_2$ have garnered interest in the last years since they appear as intermediate states in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution to $(g-2)_\mu$. Their dynamical behaviour including their transition form factors is poorly understood to this day, which also affects the uncertainty budget of the HLbL contribution. In order to improve the situation, we construct the $a_1$ and $a_2$ as resonances in the $\rho \pi$ system, which allows us to express the relevant amplitudes in terms of known form factors and properties of the resonances. With this, we aim to obtain a phenomenologically well motivated parameterisation of the transition form factors built from the general principles of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry.

title: Three-dimensional parton structure in QCD with CP-violation
summary: The Energy-Momentum tensor encodes the mechanical properties of a system such as the internal distributions energy, momentum, forces, and particle fluxes. The QCD energy momentum tensor respects CP symmetry even when QCD is modified with a CP-violating $\theta$-term. In this theory, there are 5 unique generalized form factors in the Lorentz decomposition of the total Energy Momentum tensor and 3 more which only vanish when summing over all flavors. We introduce two new lightcone GPDs whose Mellin moments give the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. These generalize the observables for QCD-based CP violation such as the neutron electric dipole moment to three dimensional light cone structure.

For Watson-admissible Gevrey clocks, the completion agrees with the canonical Borel-Laplace sum in the guaranteed directions. When the admissible aperture exceeds $2\pi$, the clockwise difference of adjacent logarithmic determinations is given by $2\pi i$ times the inverse-Mellin carrier. This carrier is also the AUF completion of a null clock and is flat on the overlap. The sum and its aggregate monodromy are thus obtained ''in one shot'', before resolving individual actions and fluctuation series. Euler's equation, zero-dimensional quartic models, the scaled Gamma function and a solvable $O(4)$ toy model exemplify the procedure, and show how further analysis recovers directional Stokes variations. The lognormal benchmark extends the construction beyond every finite Gevrey order: no finite-order Borel transform gives a convergent germ, yet explicit clock-selection conditions yield an AUF completion and a nonzero ordinary flat carrier. Distributed relaxation supplies a physical realization of this growth class. AUF therefore both reconstructs familiar resurgent information without Borel-plane continuation and extends completion beyond finite-order Borel-Laplace summation.

title: Algebra-Valued Yang-Mills-Type Theories: Polynomial Obstructions and Holonomy Reductions
summary: We study algebra-valued Yang-Mills-type ($A$-YMT) theories on a smooth $n$-manifold $M$, where connections take values in an $\mathfrak{m}$-graded algebra $(A, *)$ and descend to an associated bundle $E_A = P \times_\rho A \to M$. We derive the field equations, gauge transformations, and generalized Bianchi identities, showing that affine Ehresmann compatibility forces the vertical image of $\mathfrak{g}$ into the Lie nucleus $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Lie}}(A)$ of $[x,y]_* = x*y - y*x$, and that gauge covariance and the Bianchi identity are obstructed precisely by the Jacobiator $\mathrm{Jac}_{[\cdot,\cdot]_*}$ (leaving principal $G$-gauge symmetries anomaly-free). We then prove obstructions in three settings. First, internal-product Chern-Weil and self-dual $A$-YMT functionals vanish in weak $(2,s)$-solvable algebras, invariant under $(Q,S)$-splitting extensions. Second, in reductive Cartan-Yang-Mills theories on $A = \mathbb{R}^k \oplus \mathfrak{h}$, quartic-block parenthesization yields a strict cutoff at $n \ge 8$, while binary-tree halving yields an exact Jacobsthal-number cutoff ($n - 4 \notin \bigcup_{r \ge 3}\{2 J_r, J_{r+1}\}$, plus rank vanishing for $n \ge k + 5$). We catalog Berger holonomy reductions for $4 \le n \le 7$, proving an on-shell vanishing (torsion-free) vs. off-shell survival (torsionful) dichotomy in 4D for $U(2)$ and $SU(2)$ connections---via $e \curlywedge_\rtimes (e \curlywedge_\rtimes \Omega_\omega) = \frac{1}{2}(e \curlywedge_\rtimes e) \curlywedge_\rtimes \Omega_\omega$---and in 7D for $G_2$-connections. Third, we prove an associator-quotient collapse and Jacobiator vertex dichotomy for odd-dimensional internal $A$-Chern-Simons theories, with applications to $A$-$BF$ theories, octonionic and reductive Higgs Proca mass spectra, and reductive dualities.

title: Toward a Holographic Representation Theory of the Bosonic de Sitter Discrete Series
comment: 27 pages. Contribution to the proceedings of the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics (Group36), Valladolid, Spain, 2026
summary: We propose a program toward a holographic representation theory of the non-scalar bosonic discrete series $\Pi^\pm_{p,q}$, $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$, $1\leqslant q\leqslant p$, of the de Sitter ($\mathrm{dS}_{4}$) group $G=\mathrm{SO}_0(1,4)$. The proposal exploits two complementary realizations of the same unitary irreducible representation (UIR): a bounded-domain realization on an open ball $\mathbb{B}$ modeling the hyperbolic space $G/\mathrm{SO}(4)$, with $\partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, and a covariant spacetime realization on $\mathrm{dS}_{4}$, with conformal boundaries $\mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, in which the physical UIR is obtained through the corresponding gauge reduction. This leads to two boundary constructions and an explicit compatibility problem, \begin{align*} \mathbb{B} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \quad\overset{?}{\simeq}\quad \mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \mathrm{dS}_{4} \,. \end{align*} The two outer problems seek explicit intertwiners between the bulk and boundary realizations, with their invariant norms, constraints, and physical quotients properly identified. The middle problem asks how to construct and normalize a unitary intertwiner between the two boundary realizations once both have been shown to carry the same UIR. The bounded picture exposes the unitary and harmonic structure of the representation, while the spacetime picture makes its covariant and gauge-theoretic structure manifest, allowing the two constructions to constrain and illuminate one another. The established scalar family $\Pi_{p,0}$, $p\in\mathbb{N}$, with its spherical realization on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, provides the guiding prototype. Particular attention is given to ...

title: Remarks on Souriau's Geometric Thermodynamics for Weak Two-Dimensional Euler Flows
summary: We examine infinitesimal symmetries of relative entropy on low-regularity vorticity spaces and compare them with symmetries of stationary laws of weak two-dimensional Euler trajectories. Relative-entropy invariance under sample-space transformations is equivalent to preservation of the reference law; the corresponding weak infinitesimal condition is a vanishing reference-divergence identity. White-noise vorticity has an infinite-dimensional family of such symmetries, generated by smooth area-preserving transport. At the level of path laws, however, marginal entropy symmetries need not preserve temporal correlations. We first give a continuous Gaussian counterexample, including its infinitesimal form. We then establish a counterexample directly for stationary white-noise weak Euler path laws: explicit non-isometric area-preserving shears preserve the white-noise marginal but cannot preserve an Euler path law satisfying the standard symmetrized weak vorticity equation. We also examine the reduction of guaranteed entropy symmetries under conditioning by renormalized energy. These observations distinguish thermodynamic symmetry, Hamiltonian covariance, and statistical path dynamics without asserting a selection principle for nonunique weak solutions.

title: Polynomial integrals and Poisson structures of the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator
summary: We classify the autonomous polynomial integrals of the nondegenerate fourth-order Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator. For a rational frequency ratio $m:n$ in lowest terms, the two sector energies together with the real and imaginary parts of a single ladder product generate all polynomial integrals, subject to one defining relation. The smallest total degree of an integral not expressible through the sector energies is $m+n$, and this bound is attained. For an irrational ratio only polynomials in the sector energies are conserved. In normal-mode variables the commensurate case is the negative oscillator resonance, and the classification realizes its invariant theory in the original higher-derivative variables. Two compatible Poisson structures generate the same dynamics with an indefinite and a positive-definite Hamiltonian. They induce different brackets on the same physical generators. We show that diagonal rescalings of the generators identifying the two abstract Poisson algebras exist only when $m$ or $n$ is even, and that none of them preserves the physical domain of nonnegative sector energies. Finally, we express the generators in terms of the original coordinate and its first three derivatives. The classical multiplier identity gives their variational characteristics in closed form and shows that the additional resonant integrals cannot arise from point variational symmetries.

title: Relabeling symmetry and conservation laws in hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic upper-ocean models
comment: Submitted to Journal of Nonlinear Science. Comments welcome!
summary: We explicitly identify conserved integrals of hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic reduced-gravity upper-ocean models, both vertically unrestricted and columnar, with Noether quantities associated with particle relabeling. The columnar velocity reduction preserves the Lie-algebra structure, providing a common Euler--Poincaré framework for both families. Within this framework, we introduce nonhydrostatic columnar models with polynomial vertical buoyancy structure, extending the hydrostatic stratified hierarchy. Retaining the temporal endpoint pairing, we construct transported relabeling generators and evaluate their vorticity-dependent conserved integrals, assuming that spatial boundary terms vanish. For stratified columnar models, preservation of the effective buoyancy entering the Lagrangian suffices for symmetry even when individual buoyancy coefficients change, yielding conserved quantities that generally are not Casimirs of the full Lie--Poisson bracket. Where the Legendre transform is regular, we state the corresponding brackets and identify their Casimir families. The hydrostatic parent is treated directly through the Euler--Poincaré principle because its Legendre transform is degenerate. Integrals following directly from advection are distinguished from those obtained through the Noether pairing.

title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
summary: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

title: Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)
summary: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincaré algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.

title: Projection of massive and interacting conformal theories to the future null infinity
summary: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a Møller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.

title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde \rho$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}\psi=E\psi$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $\Sigma:=\inf\mathop{\rm this http URL} (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde \rho(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetilde\rho(r)} =-2\alpha_0, \] with $\alpha_0=\sup\{\alpha \ge 0\colon e^{2\alpha r}\widetilde \rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R_+},r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $\alpha_0^2=\Sigma-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
summary: We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity $q$ and Fermi momentum $k=(6\pi^2\rho/q)^{1/3}$, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy \[ D_{\rm M}(k)=\frac{3}{4\pi^2}\log k+O(1),\qquad D_{\rm CHF}(k)=12e^{-1/2-\pi^2/8} k^2e^{-\pi^{3/2}\sqrt{k}}(1+o(1)). \] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted $L^2$ convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

title: The Thermodynamic Limit and the Landau degeneracy
summary: Usually, thermodynamic quantities are calculated by first regularizing the system in a confining box, which may have hard walls or periodic boundaries. One then studies the finite system and takes the thermodynamic limit by letting the box grow indefinitely. Here, we discuss a regularization scheme devised in the late 1980s [1] to study the thermodynamic equations of an anyon gas [2]. Instead of confining the system with walls, the method adds a smooth harmonic potential. Quantities are evaluated in its presence, and the potential is then gradually removed. A suitable prescription for taking this limit is needed to obtain meaningful thermodynamic results.

title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
summary: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
summary: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
summary: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=\lambda \Delta +\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\delta_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $\lambda >0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(\alpha, \theta)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $\alpha\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.

title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
summary: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

title: Dynamical Gauss--Bonnet Sum Rules and Global Consistency in Five-Dimensional Braneworld Cosmology
authors: Paulo Michel Longo Tavares da Silva
summary: We derive an exact dynamical consistency relation for a smooth, periodically compactified five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet cosmology sourced by a real, minimally coupled canonical scalar field. For a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaitre--Robertson--Walker slicing and a generally time-dependent warp factor, a contraction of the bulk equations eliminates both the scalar potential and the bulk cosmological constant. A direct orthonormal-curvature reconstruction gives the independent diagonal and mixed field equations and verifies the contracted Gauss--Bonnet identity. The integrated relation separates an exact total derivative from the dynamically active Lovelock sector. Importantly, satisfying the integrated sum rule alone does not imply a solution of the complete system. We prove that, for positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling, a smooth periodic time-independent warp factor and a canonical scalar exclude all exact expanding power-law scale factors $a(t)\propto t^p$ with $p>0$. This strengthens the previously established de Sitter sign obstruction and removes an earlier interpretation of $p=1/2$ as an admissible sign-compatible physical branch. For time-dependent warping, we reformulate bouncing conditions using proper time and the physical scale factor on each constant-$y$ hypersurface. We compare the common $w=-1$ geometric member with the perturbative weighted construction of Dias, Hoff da Silva, and da Rocha. At the level of the unexpanded Ricci-trace rearrangement, the curvature-only tensor contribution differs from the full Lanczos contraction by a definite scalar-curvature term. This distinction, and the additional independent field equations, delimit the physical conclusions that may be drawn from a necessary integrated condition.

title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
summary: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

title: Destabilization of Abelian-Higgs vortices at large Chern-Simons coupling
summary: We study the effect of the Chern--Simons (CS) coupling on the radial spectral stability of axially symmetric vortices in the $(2+1)$-dimensional Abelian--Higgs model. From the linear stability approach, we obtain the dispersion relations of gauge field perturbations, which signal the existence of a critical CS coupling $k_{\rm c}$ that depends on Maxwell's coupling constant. For $k<k_{\rm c}$, the continuous spectrum is purely imaginary and the modes remain gapped. At $k=k_{\rm c}$, one of the modes becomes gapless, while for $k>k_{\rm c}$ real eigenvalues appear, corresponding to exponentially growing radial modes. Direct time-evolution simulations are consistent with the spectral analysis, which shows instability for $k>k_{\rm c}$. Below the threshold, the perturbed vortex relaxes toward its stationary profile, whereas above the threshold, growing fluctuations deform the core and propagate outward. These results show that the CS coupling controls radial spectral stability of Abelian-Higgs vortices, and destabilization occurs for sufficiently large CS coupling, relative to the Maxwell coupling.

title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

title: Geometric Quantization of the Giant Graviton Master Moduli Space
summary: We describe a remarkable reorganization of the space of gauge invariant operators of free or twisted $U(N)$ gauge theories as combinations of single-trace and determinant operators modulo certain "open loop equations". The reorganization has a transparent holographic interpretation, describing how states at finite $N$ can be reproduced by imposing certain $N$-independent gauge constraints on the combination of the closed strings Fock space and a geometric quantization of the moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes, with quantization parameter $N^{-1}$. The moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes is reproduced from tachyon condensation of auxiliary D-brane/anti-D-brane pairs which are "Koszul dual" to the D-brane system which supports the original gauge theory. We describe how to impose the open loop equations via certain BRST complexes and conjecture that their homology recovers the finite $N$ BPS Hilbert space in the limit of large auxiliary rank. The BRST construction conjecturally categorifies Murthy's Giant Graviton Expansion of indices counting $U(N)$-invariant BPS operators.

title: From pure spinor modules to superspace superfields
summary: We relate the pure spinor formalism to the superspace description of constrained superfields and gauge multiplets, mainly for abelian two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry, with three- and four-dimensional N=1 examples for comparison. For each multiplet we give an explicit module over the supertranslation Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra and match its reconstruction with the known superfields. First-order constraints come from modules supported on linear subspaces of the nilpotence variety, and higher-order ones, such as the complex-linear constraint, from Yoneda products of their Ext classes. Requiring a connection to act on given matter and its conjugate restricts its curvature, which yields the ordinary, twisted and semichiral vector multiplets with their field strengths. The module of each vector multiplet is the fiber product over the origin of the coordinate rings of the matter supports: its potentials are differences of partial potentials, and its gauge parameters are the matter superfields. For the large vector multiplet this fiber product is not a quotient of the pure spinor ring; its field strengths are four odd semichiral superfields, and partial regluing gives its constrained versions.
